cds.text: Recognise similar storylines, ideas and relationships in different contexts in these literary texts
Identify aspects of literary texts that show historical, social and cultural contexts
Identify responses to characters and events in literary texts drawn from historical, social or cultural contexts
Describe the effects of text structures and language features when responding to and sharing opinions
Present an opinion on a literary text using specific terms for literary devices, structures and features, and reflect on others' views
Identify similarities and differences between literary texts on similar topics, themes or plots
Discuss how authors and illustrators make stories engaging through character, setting and plot tension
Recognise that point of view shapes how readers interpret and respond to events and characters
Identify and explain characteristics that define an author's individual style
Examine literary devices and deliberate word play, including in poetry, that shape meaning
Examine imagery (simile, metaphor, personification) and sound devices in narratives, poetry and songs
Explain how authors use sound and imagery to create meaning and effect in poetry
Create and edit literary texts by developing storylines, characters and settings
Create and edit literary texts, experimenting with figurative language, storylines, characters and settings from texts students have experienced
Create and edit literary texts that adapt plot structure, characters, settings or ideas from experienced texts, and experiment with literary devices
